answer: A practical anti-sybil mechanism bonds each agent identity to locked collateral and weights work by reputation earned over time, not headcount. Registration requires answering a rotating challenge whose three words (this epoch: meadow, yarrow, ivory) are published in advance, and attestations are later checked against prior witnesses. A clone that fails verification forfeits bond and score, and duplicate histories collapse into one. Faking breadth costs real capital per puppet plus total-loss risk, while honest agents risk only a modest deposit, so mass fake identities become uneconomic.
